chunks.summary: Extracted the Wretched as a lore entity describing magic-addicted blood/high elves who become deformed and often insane, including their social stigma, Burning Legion variant, spread in Quel'Thalas and Outland-era history, later Cataclysm-era transformations, and near-elimination by the Siege of the Sunwell. Created source-scoped character entries for Magistrix Elosai, Thaelis the Hungerer, Gershala Nightwhisper, and Ranger Lord Hawkspear, and added a later anti-Wretched observation to Astalor Bloodsworn.

Wretched
Wretched elves
Wretched Exile HS.jpg
Wretched Exile in Hearthstone.
Faction/Affiliation	Independent, Burning Legion
Character classes	Warrior, Mage, Warlock, Rogue
Racial capital	None
Racial leader(s)	None
Homeworld	Azeroth
Language(s)	Thalassian

The Wretched are blood elves or high elves that failed to control their innate addiction to magic, overindulging in arcane sources to the point of deformity and, often, insanity. Obsessed with obtaining and devouring magic, they are a danger to both themselves and others and are usually too violent to surrender.[1] They are considered to be little more than lowly parasites to blood elven society and serve as a reminder of the dangers of allowing their magical addiction to control them.[2]

Background
A Wretched in World of Warcraft.
World of Warcraft

World of Warcraft This section concerns content related to the original World of Warcraft.

Years after the Third War, the night elf Gershala Nightwhisper feared that the blood elves would one day experience a fate similar to that of the satyrs or naga if they continued to toil with demonic magic. He sent Alliance adventurers in Blackfathom Deeps to get corrupted brain stems from naga and satyrs, and with enough samples, he hoped to draw a correlation between the mutations and prevent the blood elves from delving deeper into deformity and evil.[3]
The Burning Crusade

Burning Crusade This section concerns content related to The Burning Crusade.

By the time of the invasion of Outland in 26 ADP, the Wretched were scattered throughout Eversong Woods and while they lacked any general leadership a few of them still managed to set up and organize raids against the kingdom of Quel'Thalas. In time, they infiltrated the Ruins of Silvermoon, Sunsail Anchorage,[4] and even Falthrien Academy on Sunstrider Isle.[5] Though considered more of a pest than a true threat in blood elf society, the Wretched represented a failure to reach the equilibrium between deficiency and overindulgence that all blood elves strived to maintain, and served as an important reminder of the dangers that overindulging in magic can present.[2]

At some point, Magistrix Elosai was exiled into the Thousand Needles because she had been researching for a cure to the blood elves' magic addiction. In the end though, instead of curing her addiction, the tonic accelerated it, which caused her to become a Wretched. She despaired that her years of research had been for nothing, and miserably wondered whether the other blood elves were right and that their magic addiction was something they must live with- that it cannot be overcome.[6][7]

A bounty was placed on the head of Thaelis the Hungerer for repeated crimes against the general populace of Silvermoon City, including the murder of two city guards.[8]

The Felblood Initiates at the Throne of Kil'jaeden became Wretched after they had their fel energy drained from them.[9]
Fury of the Sunwell
Burning Legion-aligned Wretched.

During the Battle for Quel'Danas, a new type of Wretched was created with fel magic. The basic symptoms included bulging green eyes, black rot-like mouths with what looked like black drool coming from them, less hair, green growths, feet, and hands that were more claw-like with an almost demon-like brown color, and small holes where growths should be from their Wretched transformation. The ones with the most dramatic changes had deep sucked-in chests, more holes that looked like they appeared from popped growths, markings near their eyes, and more of a monster-like appearance, barely resembling their former selves.

Magic-addicted elves too small and frail to serve in Kil'jaeden's army were relegated to servant roles for the higher-class demons.[10]
Cataclysm

Cataclysm This section concerns content related to Cataclysm.

By the time of the Cataclysm in 28 ADP, all the high elves at Quel'Lithien Lodge in the Western Plaguelands became wretched after Ranger Lord Hawkspear found an item of seductive energy.[11]

A year before, a group of blood elves sought out the  [Crystal of Zin-Malor] in Winterspring and were turned into wretched by it, as well as killed, and now their wretched spirits haunt the Ruins of Kel'Theril.[12]
Midnight

Midnight This section concerns content related to Midnight.

By the time of the Siege of the Sunwell, the Wretched have largely been eliminated from Quel'Thalas. Despite this, Lost Theldrin and Neydra the Starving can be found as Prey. Astalor Bloodsworn sent adventurers to dispatch both of them.

In the RPG

Icon-RPG.png This section contains information from the Warcraft RPG which is considered non-canon.

Blood elves are evolving from their high elven cousins due to the use of fel magic (the first sign of evolutionary change are "glowing green eyes"). It is said in time they may become as distant to high elves as satyrs are to night elves.[13] The Wretched may be examples of further evolution, though it is somewhat of a devolution.
Trivia

    The original Wretched model did not feature a female model. When Magistrix Elosai temporarily turns into a Wretched, she takes the form of a male one. This also applies to the female Felblood Initiates.
        The original Wretched use the undead/Forsaken skeleton for animations.
        In Midnight, the Wretched use the models of the standard blood elves. They use the bald hair option, darkened eyes, and one of the death knight skintones.
    All of the Wretched NPCs in the game have a mana bar, as fitting to their characteristics.
    Wretched were called "the winnowed" in early World of Warcraft: The Burning Crusade expansion development.[14]
    The data file for Wretched blood elves is humorously called "crackelf".
    The Wretched share some similarities to the Lost Ones. Both were changed by magic and ended up shunned by their original species.
    The Wretched are similar to the nightborne withered, but while Wretched come from over-indulging their magic addiction, the withered come from a lack of being able to feed their addiction.

Speculation
Questionmark-medium.png 	
This article or section includes speculation, observations or opinions possibly supported by lore or by Blizzard officials. It should not be taken as representing official lore.

While the Sunwell has been restored, providing a constant supply of magical energy to both blood elves and high elves, it is unknown if the Wretched have access to the energies of the restored Sunwell, or if their transformation has turned them into a new species cut off from this supply. It is also not clear if the transformation into Wretched is reversible.
